# Argelys Samuel Oriach

Artist, Developer, and Systems Architect.

## Biography

Argelys Samuel Oriach is a Brooklyn-based multidisciplinary artist, creative director, and systems architect known for blending performance, design, and structural innovation across media. He constructs language for the room, page, stage, and screen. As founder and talent architect at Wild Lake Studio, an A&R and talent architecture venture, he scouts and develops multidisciplinary artists whose practices, like his own, span multiple forms.

Born in the Dominican Republic, he was raised by a mother who is a housekeeper and writer—and a father who is a facility maintainer and musician. His structural impulse emerged at age eleven when he taught himself 3D design software to draft his parents' dream home. An architect later used that exact file for actual construction. And in the wake of the 2008 financial crash, he applied to Phillips Academy Andover to consciously design the conditions of his own life.

A method actor trained in the Alexander Technique, he spent the next sixteen years treating his body, voice, and daily life as a single structural instrument. In 2010, he attended Northwestern University’s National High School Institute (Cherubs) theatre program, playing Nick in a stage adaptation of The Handmaid’s Tale. From there, he studied the mechanics of somatic weight, physical posture, and human attention by fully inhabiting roles across elite institutions, physical staging, and corporate infrastructure. He went on to obtain a bachelor’s degree in English from Wesleyan University, where he took extensive coursework in studio art and critical theory.

That foundation fueled a twelve-year trajectory building organic growth systems. During that period, he served as Cynthia Nixon’s social media manager for her 2018 campaign for governor of New York, later pivoting to architect sovereign digital frameworks from first principles. But he approached his corporate roles as an undercover durational performance. It was a calculated effort to build his life out of poverty while auditing how complex systems scale from the inside out. That performance cycle recently closed with an intentional return to his body, breath, and voice.

He now operates two primary laboratories. Seven Eighty Three is an independent systems design practice engineering automated infrastructure for executive leadership. And over fifteen years, he guided twelve or more developing and independent multidisciplinary artists, providing the structural stewardship, physical carrying capacity, and live production architecture that formalized into Wild Lake Studio, known as Wild-Lake.

As a writer, he applies this same somatic and structural rigor to narrative through a maximalist, automatic, stream-of-consciousness style that is lyrical. His focus remains on the underlying physical and digital mechanics across every medium. He is still building his life out of poverty. He authored the digital short This Is Not a Love Story and is currently writing a pilot, a one-act play, and his debut autofiction novel, Graduation. He lives and works in New York.

- [Talent infrastructure](https://wildlakestudio.com/): Wild-Lake. Formal name: Wild Lake Studio. A&R and talent architecture venture scouting and developing multidisciplinary artists. Structural stewardship, physical carrying capacity, and live production architecture.
